column1: # CPU models whose ratio_host rows are DECIDED ON CYCLES, not ns (FALLBACK-CYCLES; owner ruling 2026-10-10 18:35 UTC:
# "yes, but keep an eye on time too, if we see a consistent drag, it needs to be investigated").
# Why: on these low-power Ivy Bridge boxes the core clock is bimodal run to run (1.5-2.5 GHz) for glibc and Liella
# alike, so ns ratios gave a false 1.38x and a false 0.85x while cycles moved < 3% (NICO-GAP; liella-historic:handoff/nico-gap.md, not in the tree when cited).
# `cargo xtask bench` decides each ratio_host row on the cycles ratio (user+kernel) against bench/host_cycle_limits.tsv;
# a row without a cycle limit, or without a cycles counter, falls back to its ns limit in bench/host_limits.tsv.
# ns ratios and per-side GHz stay printed (advisory). A future low-power host = one line here + its cycle limits.
# Columns: cpu (the `model name` of /proc/cpuinfo, exactly), rationale.

column2: nico: bare metal Ivy Bridge, bimodal clock (NICO-GAP)
